text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help pinpoint the cause of your fatigue and itching, can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or if your urine has become dark?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, have you experienced any pale or clay-colored stools, or noticed a recent unintentional weight loss? I also need to know if you consume alcohol regularly or use any new medications or herbal supplements.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, the presence of scleral icterus, and severe pruritus, I suspect a cholestatic liver disease. REQUEST TEST: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies (AMA) and Liver Biopsy.

text: RESULTS: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies (AMA): Negative. Liver Biopsy: Not performed (not available in data).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the AMA test is negative, Primary Biliary Cholangitis is unlikely, so I need to consider Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, which is strongly associated with your ulcerative colitis. REQUEST TEST: Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP).

speaker: Measurement

text: Since MRCP is unavailable, I will proceed with standard liver imaging and viral hepatitis screening to rule out other causes of cholestasis and hepatocellular injury. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound, Hepatitis B and C serology, and IgG levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of bile duct thickening and dilatation, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis, strongly point to Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
